title: Trek through the South and Texas; buying pot, change of trains at El Paso
summary: After the Royal and Howard Theatres the band does a long one-nighter run through Texas, where musicians stock up on cheap marijuana.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: January of 1945 is when Fats Navarro joins us, and we started our trek South. We played again the Royal Theatre in Baltimore, the Howard Theatre in Washington, D.C., and then we went points South, not missing a state. We played a couple of places in Virginia, Richmond I think, and somewhere else. Then we went to North South Carolina and played two or three places there, then South Carolina, Georgia. Of course, we played Jacksonville, Florida, and Miami and Tampa. As a matter of fact, we had a very long one-nighter schedule that went all the way down to Florida, then across through Alabama and Louisiana, and into Texas.

We stayed in Texas I guess about a week, playing different places, because Texas is so big, and there are so many towns there that you can play. Houston, Dallas, San Anton, Fort Worth, and two or three other places. Anyway, it was always good to be down there, because we were very well received.

From Texas, we headed for Los Angeles. That's where another thing happened. In Texas, we could always load up... You know, guys who smoked pot could always load up on it in Texas. It was very cheap. You could buy something like a

whole pound of pot for thirty some dollars or something like that. So we ran into this guy down there, and everybody just loaded up. Some guys had pounds, half-pounds, quarter-pounds, whatever. Heh. I believe it was in Dallas or San Anton or someplace where this happened.

And we left there, and we caught the train and went down to this little border town across from Juarez, Mexico -- El Paso, Texas. That's where, during those days, you would change trains to go to Los Angeles or points West. So we get to El Paso, you change trains, and we have a wait for the next train of about three hours. So everybody, in a situation like that, you always put your bags in a locker or something and go around, and see what's happening in the town or whatever, and just find a way to kill three hours until the train comes.
